summary: Discovery-style security review focusing on SAML and SCIM provisioning patterns and an incremental least-privilege RBAC rollout. Customer wants to understand: how SAML role/assertion maps into Redwood console roles, group sync cadence and reconciliation for SCIM, audit log locations and retention policies, and KMS support for encryption at rest. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 and SCIM mapping examples; run a SCIM sync test in Verdant staging; customer to provide existing role mappings to plan pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Ariel Gomez (Verdant Head of Platform), Samir Patel (Verdant Security Eng), Laura Kim (Verdant IAM), Ben O'Connor (Verdant Infra)

[00:00] Jesse Park: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Jesse, AE for Redwood, Maya is our systems engineer, Omar's on CSM. We wanted to walk through your SSO/SCIM provisioning model and the role-binding approach you sketched in the doc.
[00:18] Ariel Gomez: Thanks, Jesse. I have Laura and Samir from security; Ben's here for infra questions. High level, we run Azure AD as IdP and we've got a mix of on-prem and cloud accounts. We're trying to avoid giving blanket admin rights in Redwood console.
[00:35] Maya Chen: Totally. So the main things we'll cover: SP vs IdP initiated SAML flows, attribute mappings for roles, SCIM group sync cadence and reconciliation, how audit logs surface, and options for KMS.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Quick question before we dig in — do you have an IdP metadata import flow or is it manual? We use conditional access in AAD and rotate certs quarterly.
[01:07] Jesse Park: You can import IdP metadata or upload certs manually. We also support automated cert rotation via metadata refresh, but for AAD many customers do a manual cert swap during scheduled windows.
[01:20] Ben O'Connor: Are there any gotchas for SP-initiated vs IdP-initiated for provisioning? We prefer SP-initiated to lock flows to the app.
[01:31] Maya Chen: SP-initiated is fine; provisioning (SCIM) is separate. For provisioning you'll configure a SCIM connector on the IdP side (Azure AD) pointing to Redwood's SCIM endpoint. The SAML flow choice doesn't affect SCIM behavior, but if you rely on SAML attributes for role mapping you'll want consistent assertion content for both flows.
[01:55] Laura Kim: On role mapping — can Redwood consume a SAML attribute like roles or appRole to map to console roles?
[02:04] Maya Chen: Yes. We support extracting attributes from the SAML assertion — common claims are 'roles', 'appRoles', or a custom attribute. In the console you can map claim values to a Redwood role (example: 'redwood_admin' -> Admin). We also support using the 'groups' claim and SCIM-provisioned groups for more scalable mapping.
[02:28] Ariel Gomez: What's the recommended pattern for least-privilege? We have several teams that need narrow permissions to only a subset of projects/environments.
[02:38] Maya Chen: Best practice is group-based roles: have Azure AD groups per product-team-environment and assign those groups to Redwood roles via SCIM group sync. That way membership changes in AD are the single source of truth. Also use scoped roles (we support project-scoped role bindings) to limit admin surfaces.
[02:58] Samir Patel: How does SCIM handle reconciliation? If we remove a user from an AD group, how quickly does Redwood remove the role?
[03:07] Maya Chen: SCIM supports incremental sync and full sync. Default cadence is delta every 5 minutes for high-throughput customers, but for hosted customers it may be every 15 minutes depending on rate limits. On a delta removal, we reconcile and remove the role within the next sync window; you can also trigger a manual reconcile via the API/Console.
[03:32] Jesse Park: Note that for Dedicated or Private deployments we can adjust sync cadence to be more aggressive if you need near-real-time revocation.
[03:42] Ben O'Connor: Good to know. Audit logs — where do they live for hosted vs private? Retention?
[03:50] Omar Ruiz: For hosted customers we store audit logs in our managed log storage with default retention 90 days; you can purchase extended retention. For dedicated/private deployments we support streaming audit logs to your S3 bucket or SIEM via HTTPS forwarder with retention controlled by your own policies.
[04:11] Samir Patel: Are logs immutable? We need tamper-evident storage for compliance.
[04:17] Maya Chen: Logs are write-once in our managed cloud tier — tamper-evident through append-only storage with integrity checks. For Private deployments, since the customer controls retention destination, you'd configure immutability there (S3 Object Lock or your SIEM's WORM config).
[04:37] Laura Kim: Encryption and KMS — can we bring our own KMS? We need customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted customers can opt-in for CMEK with partner-managed HSMs in supported regions — we have integrations for AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and HashiCorp Vault for dedicated partners. Key rotation is configurable and we provide key-rotation docs.
[05:06] Ariel Gomez: Any restrictions on key algorithms? We run RSA-2048 and AES-256 for envelopes.
[05:12] Maya Chen: AES-256 envelope encryption is standard; we support RSA and ECDSA for signing of certificates. We'll share the KMS compatibility matrix.
[05:20] Jesse Park: Back to SCIM — on attributes, do you need custom mapping? Many customers map 'mail'->email, 'displayName'->name, and 'memberOf'->groups. Anything custom?
[05:30] Samir Patel: We have a custom attribute 'app_roles' in AAD with comma-separated values.
[05:36] Maya Chen: We can parse a comma-delimited attribute and map each value to a console role. It will require a small transformation script during provisioning or a SCIM mapping rule; I'll include an example in the follow-up.
[05:49] Ben O'Connor: Group sync volume — we have ~25k users and ~1.2k groups. Any rate-limit and performance notes?
[05:58] Maya Chen: For large directories, we recommend Dedicated or Private due to sync throughput and delta handling. Our hosted tier supports large orgs but performance will depend on sync window and rate limits. For delta syncs we page through group members; for bulk imports we recommend an initial full import window off-hours.
[06:20] Ariel Gomez: If we do an initial full import, can we do a dry-run to see expected role assignments?
[06:27] Maya Chen: Yes — we have a SCIM dry-run mode that returns the mapping results without applying role grants. We'll run that in staging during the sync test.
[06:38] Samir Patel: On RBAC design, how granular are roles? Do you support resource-level permissions?
[06:45] Maya Chen: Yes — roles can be global or scoped to specific projects/environments. You can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions (read logs, deploy model, manage keys, etc.). Role bindings can reference groups, users, or service accounts.
[06:59] Laura Kim: Service accounts — can they be issued via SCIM or only created manually/API? We want service accounts for CI pipelines and limited lifetime creds.
[07:08] Maya Chen: Service accounts are created via the API/Console; we support short-lived tokens and automatic key rotation for service accounts. We don't provision service accounts via SCIM because SCIM is user-focused — but you can provision a dedicated user that we treat as a machine account and then exchange creds for short-lived tokens.
[07:33] Jesse Park: Quick check — do you have any regulatory data residency constraints?
[07:38] Ariel Gomez: Yes, European customer data must stay in EU regions for certain teams. We also have some Canadian clients requiring CA residency.
[07:46] Maya Chen: Redwood supports region pinning for data residency. For hosted accounts you can choose region for storage and model execution; for Private you can deploy within your VPC/region. We'll document region compliance pages for EU/CA.
[08:02] Samir Patel: What about cross-region replication of logs? We want backups in a separate region but log copies must be encrypted and access-controlled.
[08:12] Omar Ruiz: Cross-region replication is supported but must be configured explicitly. For hosted, replication destinations are encrypted and access-controlled; for Private you'll manage replication controls. We can show options in the SOC 2 docs.
[08:31] Ben O'Connor: On onboarding lifecycle — new hires, ladders, contractors — what's a recommended sync strategy?
[08:38] Maya Chen: Use group lifecycle management on your IdP: onboard to AD groups, SCIM sync will pick it up and apply role grants. For contractors, a best practice is time-bound group membership or join/leave automation tied to HR systems. We support SCIM push for provisioning and deprovisioning to ensure timely revocation.
[09:00] Ariel Gomez: If someone is removed mid-day, is there a way to force immediate logout or token revocation for active sessions?
[09:08] Maya Chen: Yes. You can revoke sessions via the Console or call the sessions-revoke API. For SAML session durations, we recommend short session TTLs for sensitive roles and coupling revocation to SCIM reconciliation for near-real-time enforcement. For Dedicated/private we can shorten token TTLs further.
[09:29] Samir Patel: How detailed are audit logs for admin actions? We need to show who changed RBAC bindings, who rotated keys, who triggered a rollback.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Audit logs capture user, timestamp, action, resource, and request metadata including IP and agent. For admin-level changes we include before/after diffs for role bindings and key rotations. Logs are queryable in the Console and exportable via API.
[09:58] Laura Kim: Is there an event we can hook into for compliance alerts? For example, a privileged role change should trigger an alert to our SIEM.
[10:06] Omar Ruiz: Yes — we support webhook notifications for defined events and direct SIEM forwarding. You can also stream logs to S3 and have your SIEM ingest them.
[10:20] Jesse Park: On cert rotation for SAML, any automatic notification before expiry?
[10:25] Maya Chen: We send automated notifications 30/14/7 days before cert expiry, and the metadata includes next-rotation window. For AAD, you can set up auto-renewal of app certs in some flows, but many customers do a manual swap during maintenance windows.
[10:41] Ariel Gomez: For the SCIM connector, what auth modes do you support? OAuth bearer, basic auth?
[10:47] Maya Chen: SCIM supports OAuth2 bearer tokens (recommended) and token rotation; for some legacy setups we allow basic token auth but advise against it. We also support IP allowlists and private VPC endpoints for SCIM traffic.
[11:03] Ben O'Connor: Private endpoints — can we restrict SCIM to an internal endpoint only accessible from our VPC?
[11:09] Maya Chen: For Private deployments yes; for hosted we provide VPC peering or static IP ranges and an option to set up a customer-managed NAT to restrict traffic. We also support mTLS for SCIM endpoints on request.
[11:28] Samir Patel: Let's talk specifics of mapping the 'app_roles' custom attribute — we want two Redwood roles: 'deploy' and 'observer'. The attribute is comma separated.
[11:37] Maya Chen: Example mapping: parse 'app_roles' -> split by comma -> trim -> map each token to Redwood role. I'll include a JSON mapping snippet. In the console you can also set fallback roles for unmapped tokens.
[11:56] Jesse Park: We should also highlight the canary approach for least-privilege: start with a single team, run the SCIM dry-run, validate access patterns, then expand.
[12:05] Ariel Gomez: Agreed. We'll pilot with the analytics team first.
[12:09] Laura Kim: For the dry-run, can we get logs of expected denies/perm changes?
[12:15] Maya Chen: Yes — dry-run outputs include expected grants and denies with context for the API/Console calls that would have been executed.
[12:26] Ben O'Connor: Compliance — do you do ISO 27001? Some of our customers ask for it in addition to SOC 2.
[12:33] Jesse Park: Redwood has SOC 2; ISO 27001 is on the roadmap and we can share the current control mappings and timelines.
[12:43] Samir Patel: Any backdoors or access patterns from Redwood staff into dedicated/private? What's the escalation for support needing access?
[12:53] Omar Ruiz: For hosted, Redwood staff access is via least-privileged support roles and time-bound session elevation; all access is logged and requires request approvals. For Private, we only get access if you provide explicit temporary access (bastion/key) or we do guided sessions. We can put those processes in writing.
[13:13] Laura Kim: What about SCIM schema extensions? We have custom attributes like 'employeeType' and 'costCenter'. Can those be pushed and stored?
[13:22] Maya Chen: We store custom attributes as part of the user profile and you can use them in mapping rules. We persist them in the profile store and they appear on the user object in logs for debugging.
[13:34] Jesse Park: Are there any risk areas we should call out for the pilot?
[13:40] Maya Chen: Main risks: mismatched claim names causing role misassignments, large group sync causing throttling if run at peak, and stale session tokens if you rely only on session TTLs. Mitigations: dry-run, staggered bulk import, short session TTLs for initial rollout, and manual reconciliation API.
[13:58] Ariel Gomez: Let's talk about delegation — some teams need to manage access themselves. Can Redwood's RBAC allow team admins limited to their project?
[14:07] Maya Chen: Yes — you can create delegated admin roles scoped to resources. Delegated admins can manage members within their scope but cannot bump themselves to platform admin.
[14:21] Samir Patel: How about SCIM failures? If a user is created but mapping fails, do you have an error queue?
[14:29] Maya Chen: We have a provisioning error dashboard that surfaces mapping errors with payload and recommended remediations. You can retry individual items or re-run a full sync.
[14:42] Ben O'Connor: For tokens used by CI, can we limit token scopes and TTLs?
[14:47] Maya Chen: Yes — service tokens can be scoped to APIs and have TTLs; you can set automated rotation and restrict origin IPs.
[14:58] Jesse Park: I'm going to recap the agreed follow-ups so we have clarity.
[15:03] Jesse Park: Redwood will send SOC 2, SCIM mapping examples including parsing the 'app_roles' attribute, and guidance on KMS compatibility. Verdant will provide a sample group/user CSV and the desired mapping for the pilot. We'll schedule a SCIM dry-run in your staging IdP next week.
[15:18] Ariel Gomez: Sounds good. Any other open items?
[15:20] Laura Kim: One last Q — can we restrict who can create API keys in the console?
[15:24] Maya Chen: Yes — API key creation is controlled by a permission bit; you can have role-based controls to limit who can create and rotate keys.
[15:32] Samir Patel: Also, we'd like logs forwarded to Splunk — do you have a connector?
[15:36] Omar Ruiz: We support Splunk HEC and can provide the ingestion spec and examples.
[15:42] Ben O'Connor: Ok great. If we do the pilot and it looks good, what's the path to production and SLA changes?
[15:49] Jesse Park: Pilot -> Dedicated reserved capacity or Private deployment depending on scale and compliance. SLA tiers available for Dedicated. We'll include pricing and SLA options in the follow-up email.
[16:01] Ariel Gomez: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll get our CSV and map over the week.
[16:05] Jesse Park: Thanks everyone. We'll send the docs and schedule the SCIM test.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, speaker overlap around 11:00-12:00, some proper nouns transcribed imperfectly (e.g., 'Verdant' sometimes heard as 'variant' by auto-transcriber).
closure_notes: Recap: Redwood to share SOC 2/ISO summary, SCIM mapping examples (including app_roles parse), KMS compatibility, and Splunk ingestion spec. Verdant to provide group CSV and required AAD attributes. Schedule SCIM dry-run for staging next week. Follow-up email to confirm dates.
